clue.text: Old tree with leafy hollow

parts.note: the elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

indicators.note: hollow means the inside of the word leafy is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of leafy

explanation.surface: A description of an ancient tree beside a leafy dip in a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' looks like a noun for a dip in the ground, but it says to empty leafy, keeping L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly person is getting on in years, so the word is a synonym for aged.

clue.text: Criminal ruins fellow rebel

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of ruins are bent into a new order

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker brings down a man who has risen up against authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging RUINS gives INSUR, then GENT is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is someone who rises in armed revolt against the government, so a rebel.

clue.text: From time to time, Orwell is hard to enjoy

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then means every other letter of Orwell

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of Orwell
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A reader admits George Orwell's books are a struggle to like.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Orwell is thinned out by 'From time to time', giving REL; IS is taken as written and H stands for hard, as on pencils.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to take great pleasure in it, a close synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Dog destroyed atlas at home, eating America

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters of atlas are scrambled
eating means one piece swallows the other, so the A goes inside

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'is she in?'

explanation.surface: A pet dog chews up the family atlas, devouring the map of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' turns ATLAS into ALSAT; 'eating' puts A (America) inside IN (at home), giving IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian is the British name for the German shepherd breed.

clue.text: So psychiatrists confused scientists

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled, so all the letters of so psychiatrists are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that psychiatrists have baffled other researchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrophysicists study the physics of stars and space, so they are one kind of scientist.

clue.text: Mistake by staff taking a way off the motorway

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake

indicators.note: taking means the rod takes in the letter A, holding it inside

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: An error by highway staff sends a driver down the wrong exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts A inside ROD to make ROAD. A slip road is the British term for a ramp leaving or joining a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is a short exit or entry ramp, the road by which traffic leaves a motorway.

clue.text: In France you originally located interesting pink flower

parts.note: tu is French for you

indicators.note: originally points to the start of each of the next three words

parts.note: first letter of located
first letter of interesting
first letter of pink

explanation.surface: A tourist in France finds a remarkable pink bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: TU is the familiar French word for you; 'originally' takes L, I and P.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring bulb plant with a cup-shaped bloom.

clue.text: Maybe painting is beginning to attract new craftsperson

parts.note: painting is one example of art, hence 'maybe'

indicators.note: beginning to points at the first letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of attract

explanation.surface: A painting starts to win attention for a fresh maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker who makes things by hand, a craftsperson.

clue.text: Pressure breathing apparatus before base dive

indicators.note: before puts the lung ahead of the base letter

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
a lung is the organ we breathe with
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A diver checks the air pressure in their breathing kit before leaving base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathing apparatus' suggests scuba gear, but it is the body's own lung; E as base is a mathematical convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to jump or dive headlong into water.

clue.text: Short journey allows some music

parts.note: a trip is a short journey
lets means allows

explanation.surface: A brief outing permits a little music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, triplets are groups of three notes played in the time of two, so a passage of music.

clue.text: I clear up badly — that's odd

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of I clear up are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who tidies poorly notices something strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar means strange or unusual, so an odd thing is peculiar.

clue.text: Calm salesman is in debt, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are heard rather than read, so it is a soundalike

parts.note: a rep (sales representative) owes money: REP OWES

explanation.surface: A tranquil travelling salesman is said to owe money.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a state of rest or tranquillity, a noun synonym of calm.

clue.text: Victory perhaps tires part of body

parts.note: to flag is to tire, so flags means tires
the hip is a part of the body

explanation.surface: Winning, maybe, wears out one part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victory' is HMS Victory, Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, not a win; 'tires' is the verb, not wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Victory was the leading ship of Nelson's fleet, an example of a flagship.

clue.text: Holding on to advertising space

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as in keeping and stockpiling
second meaning: a large board for posters, a billboard

explanation.surface: A company clings to its billboard slot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stockpiling things and a large outdoor board for posters.

clue.text: Stylish chap picked up large cat and plant

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so it is a soundalike

parts.note: a dandy is a stylish, well-dressed chap
the lion is a large cat

explanation.surface: A well-dressed man lifts a big cat and a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' means heard: DANDY said aloud gives the start of the plant's name, and LION follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a common yellow-flowered weed, a type of plant.

clue.text: European wearing headgear greeting period of high temperature

indicators.note: wearing means the E has the hat on it, so it sits inside

parts.note: a hat is headgear
a wave is a greeting

explanation.surface: A tourist in a sunhat waves hello during a hot spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A heatwave is a spell of unusually hot weather lasting several days.

clue.text: Lacking energy, like an unprepared shopper?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: ..., a shopper with no shopping list

explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lethargic and without enthusiasm; split up, it describes being without a shopping list.

clue.text: Affect with emotion in part of church

parts.note: a spire is the tall pointed tower on a church

explanation.surface: A worshipper is moved by something inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is to fill someone with a feeling, such as enthusiasm or awe.

clue.text: Set up trendy street area on the outskirts of Liverpool

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: the outskirts of a city are its edges, so take the first and last letters of Liverpool

parts.note: first and last letters of Liverpool

explanation.surface: Someone establishes a fashionable street district at the edge of Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outskirts of' looks like geography, but it takes L and L from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to put it in place and make it ready, to set it up.

clue.text: Occurrence with popular detectives sent to depose leader

parts.note: in means popular, as in 'the in crowd'
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

indicators.note: deposing the leader removes the first letter of sent

explanation.surface: Popular detectives are dispatched to oust a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police; sent loses S.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an event or happening, a synonym for occurrence.

clue.text: Some fracas in old gambling location

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out in a seedy old gaming house.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where people play games of chance for money.

clue.text: View some multimedia spectacular

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch part of a lavish multimedia show.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the outlook or prospect a place offers, as in a room with a southern aspect.

clue.text: Headless monster making mistake

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of terror is cut off

parts.note: a terror is a frightful person or creature, a monster

explanation.surface: A beast without a head is a blunder in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Seal unit possibly to keep warm

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters of seal unit

explanation.surface: Instructions to seal a unit in order to retain heat.
explanation.definitionFit: To insulate is to wrap something so heat cannot escape, keeping it warm.

clue.text: Wrongly interprets dreams — is in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so the letters of dreams and is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dream analyst gets meanings wrong and ends up in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To misread something is to understand or interpret it incorrectly.

clue.text: Improvise with pasta

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to play music in an improvised, casual way
second meaning: a strip of pasta

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests making do in the kitchen; the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for idle musical improvising and a noun for a strip of pasta.

clue.text: Unrivalled — like the House of Commons?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: ..., the Commons has no peers, who sit in the Lords

explanation.walkthrough: Peers are members of the House of Lords; the elected House of Commons has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means matchless, having no equal; read as peer-less it describes a chamber without nobles.
